question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

The speech you made today was sillier and irrelevant.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. silly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When two adjectives describing the same noun are joined by "and", both must be in the same degree. Here "irrelevant" is in the positive degree, so the first adjective must also be positive — "silly", not the comparative "sillier".

◦ Correct: The speech you made today was silly and irrelevant.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "silliest" (superlative) and Option 3 "most silly" break the parallelism with "irrelevant" and there is no comparison with "than" in the sentence.

• Option 4 "more silly" is a comparative; moreover, short adjectives like "silly" form the comparative with "-er" (sillier), not with "more".

NOTE

• Parallelism rule: adjectives joined by "and/or" must match in degree — "silly and irrelevant" (both positive), "sillier and more irrelevant" (both comparative). Degrees of silly: silly – sillier – silliest.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

She showed this plant and talked about it's medicinal properties.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. its medicinal properties.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Its" (without an apostrophe) is the possessive form of "it", while "it's" is the contraction of "it is / it has". The sentence needs the possessive — the plant's properties — so "its medicinal properties" is correct.

◦ Correct: She showed this plant and talked about its medicinal properties.

• "Medicinal" (having healing properties — औषधीय) is the right word for a plant's healing qualities; "medical" relates to the science/practice of medicine.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "their" is a plural pronoun and cannot refer to the singular "plant"; it also wrongly uses "medical".

• Options 3 and 4 retain the wrong contraction "it's"; Option 3 also uses "proprieties" (correct social behaviour), a different word from "properties" (qualities).

NOTE

• Common confusions: its (possessive) vs it's (it is); medicinal (having curative value — medicinal plants) vs medical (related to the field of medicine — medical college); property (quality) vs propriety (decorum).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Diligent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Industrious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Diligent" means hardworking; showing steady, careful and persistent effort. Its closest synonym is "industrious" (hardworking). (परिश्रमी / मेहनती)

◦ Example: The diligent/industrious student revised her notes every day and topped the exam.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Lazy" (unwilling to work) is the antonym of diligent.

• Option 3 "Noisy" (making a lot of sound) and Option 4 "Positive" (optimistic) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of diligent: industrious, hardworking, assiduous, sedulous, conscientious, painstaking. Antonyms: lazy, idle, indolent, negligent.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the given word.

Merciful
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cruel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Merciful" means showing mercy, kindness or forgiveness. Its antonym is "cruel", meaning causing pain or suffering without pity. (दयालु का विलोम — निर्दयी/क्रूर)

◦ Example: The merciful king pardoned the prisoner, but his cruel brother wanted him punished.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Cunning" (crafty/sly) is unrelated to mercy.

• Option 2 "Mild" (gentle) is closer to a synonym of merciful.

• Option 4 "Magical" (relating to magic) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of merciful: compassionate, kind, lenient, forgiving, clement. Antonyms: cruel, merciless, ruthless, pitiless, brutal.

question:
The given sentence is divided into three segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

She learnt / how to play a piano / when she was in Class 6th.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. how to play a piano.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Names of musical instruments take the definite article "the" when we talk about playing them. So it should be "how to play the piano", not "a piano".

◦ Correct: She learnt how to play the piano when she was in Class 6th.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "She learnt" (correct past tense; "learnt" is the British past form of "learn") and "when she was in Class 6th" are grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Article rule: use "the" with musical instruments — play the piano/violin/guitar/flute. But games and sports take no article — play cricket, play chess (NOT "play the cricket").

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'isolated' from the given sentence.

A Greek mythological story says that Echo was the most beautiful nymph who lived in the lovely and lonely mountains of Greece and is believed to be garrulous too.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Lonely.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Isolated" means far away from other places/people; remote, solitary. In the sentence, the word "lonely" (unfrequented, solitary — describing the mountains) is its closest synonym. (एकाकी / निर्जन)

◦ In "the lovely and lonely mountains of Greece", "lonely" describes mountains that are remote and isolated.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Garrulous" means excessively talkative (बातूनी) — unrelated to isolation.

• Option 3 "Beautiful" and Option 4 "Lovely" describe attractiveness, not remoteness.

NOTE

• Synonyms of isolated: lonely, remote, secluded, solitary, cut-off. Antonyms: accessible, crowded, connected. In vocabulary-from-context questions, always match the meaning of the given word with the words actually present in the sentence.

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

She always wears a bizzare combination of clothes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Bizarre.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "bizarre", meaning very strange or unusual; odd. (विचित्र / अजीब)

◦ Correct: She always wears a bizarre combination of clothes.

• Spelling key: BI + ZARRE — one "z" and double "r", ending in "-e".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Bizzare", "Bizaar", "Bizzar" and "Bizare" are all misspellings.

• Do not confuse "bizarre" (strange) with "bazaar" (a market — बाज़ार).

NOTE

• Synonyms of bizarre: strange, weird, odd, peculiar, outlandish. Antonyms: normal, ordinary, usual, conventional.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The act of transferring one's authority to another
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Delegation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Delegation" means the act of transferring/entrusting one's authority, power or work to another person. (अधिकारों का प्रत्यायोजन)

◦ Example: Delegation of authority by a manager allows subordinates to take decisions on his behalf.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Mediary" (an intermediary/go-between) is a person, not an act.

• Option 2 "Agency" is the business/office of an agent, not the act of transferring authority.

• Option 3 "Assignee" is the person to whom a right or property is transferred, not the act itself.

NOTE

• Related words: delegate (verb — to entrust; noun — a representative), delegation (the act of entrusting authority; also a group of representatives). One-word substitutes are frequently asked in SSC exams — learn them with their exact definitions.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

“It’s really __________ to incorporate changes at the last minute,” she said.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. difficult.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After "It's really ___ to + verb", we need an adjective modified by the adverb "really". "Difficult" (adjective — hard to do) fits perfectly.

◦ Correct: "It's really difficult to incorporate changes at the last minute," she said.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "difficulty" and Option 2 "difficulties" are nouns — a noun cannot follow "really" in this structure.

• Option 4 "most difficult" (superlative) needs "the" and a comparison group; it does not fit here.

NOTE

• Structure: It + is + adjective + to-infinitive — "It is difficult/easy/impossible to do something." Note the word family: difficult (adjective), difficulty (noun), difficultly (rare adverb).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

Despite the setbacks, the team decided to persevere and keep working on the project, believing it could be a _______ for their company.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. game-changer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "game-changer" is something that completely changes a situation, bringing a decisive/positive transformation. The team believed the project could transform the company's fortunes. (परिस्थिति को पूरी तरह बदल देने वाली चीज़)

◦ Correct: ... believing it could be a game-changer for their company.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "beat around the bush" means to avoid coming to the main point.

• Option 3 "needle in a haystack" means something almost impossible to find.

• Option 4 "wild goose chase" means a hopeless, futile search — none of these fits the positive sense required.

NOTE

• Idioms of success/decisive impact: "game-changer", "turn the tables", "a shot in the arm" (a boost), "turning point".

question:
Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank.

The judge declared that the red car went ___________ than the blue car.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. farther.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" requires the comparative degree. The comparative of "far" is "farther" (used for physical distance).

◦ Correct: The red car went farther than the blue car.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "more far" is incorrect — "far" has the irregular comparative "farther/further", never "more far".

• Option 3 "far" (positive degree) cannot be used with "than".

• Option 4 "farthest" is the superlative, used with "the", not with "than".

NOTE

• Degrees: far – farther/further – farthest/furthest. "Farther" is preferred for physical distance; "further" also means "additional" (further information). Irregular comparatives: good–better–best, bad–worse–worst, little–less–least.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

It is worth noting that the possible from him being voted as the class monitor is next to zero.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. possibility of him.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the article "the", a noun is required — "possibility" (noun), not "possible" (adjective) or "possibly" (adverb). The noun "possibility" takes the preposition "of".

◦ Correct: ... the possibility of him being voted as the class monitor is next to zero.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "possibility at him" uses the wrong preposition — "possibility" takes "of", not "at".

• Option 2 "possibly of him" wrongly uses an adverb after "the".

• Option 4 "possible of him" wrongly uses an adjective as a noun.

NOTE

• Word family: possible (adjective) – possibly (adverb) – possibility (noun). Fixed pairing: "the possibility of + noun/gerund" — "the possibility of winning/of him being selected". "Next to zero" = almost nil.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the highlighted words in the given sentence.

His sudden departure left us in a difficult situation; it was like he suddenly took away important support from us.
option_2: hit the nail on the head
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. pulled the rug out.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "pull the rug out (from under someone)" means to suddenly take away important support or help from someone, leaving them in a difficult position. (अचानक सहारा छीन लेना)

◦ Correct: His sudden departure left us in a difficult situation; it was like he pulled the rug out from under us.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "hit the nail on the head" means to say/do exactly the right thing.

• Option 3 "got his act together" means organised oneself to work effectively.

• Option 4 "hit the sack" means to go to bed — none of these matches "took away important support".

NOTE

• Idioms of betrayal/sudden loss of support: "pull the rug out from under someone", "leave someone in the lurch", "stab someone in the back".

question: Select the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Embarrassment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Embarrassment" is correctly spelt. It means a feeling of shame, awkwardness or self-consciousness. (शर्मिंदगी / झेंप)

• Spelling key: EM + BARRASS + MENT — double "r" AND double "s".

◦ Example: His face turned red with embarrassment when he forgot his speech.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options are misspelt: "Ocassion" → occasion (double "c", single "s"), "Acommodate" → accommodate (double "c" and double "m"), "Recieve" → receive ("i before e except after c").

NOTE

• Frequently tested spellings in SSC exams: occasion, accommodate, receive, embarrassment, committee, millennium, questionnaire, necessary. Learn the double-letter patterns carefully.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

An axe to grind
option_2: To tackle a problem in a bold and direct fashion
option_4: To have a selfish reason that influences the actions
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To have a selfish reason that influences the actions.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "an axe to grind" means to have a private/selfish motive or personal interest behind one's actions. (निजी स्वार्थ होना)

◦ Example: He criticised the new policy, but many suspect he has an axe to grind because it affects his own business.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Bitterly hostile" matches idioms like "at daggers drawn".

• Option 2 "To tackle a problem in a bold and direct fashion" matches "take the bull by the horns".

• Option 3 "To make a supreme effort" matches "move heaven and earth" — none of these is the meaning of "an axe to grind".

NOTE

• Related idioms: "feather one's own nest" (act for selfish gain), "have a vested interest", "grind one's own axe". Idiom meanings are directly asked in SSC CGL/CHSL/MTS — learn them with example sentences.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Cuorse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cuorse" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "course", meaning a route/direction, a series of lessons, or a part of a meal. (पाठ्यक्रम / मार्ग)

◦ Example: She joined a computer course after school.

• Spelling key: C + OURSE — "ou" before "r", not "uo".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Necessary" (one "c", double "s"), "Consider" (to think about) and "Personal" (private, individual) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "course" (path/lessons — a course of action) with "coarse" (rough in texture — coarse cloth). Homophones like course/coarse are common in SSC spelling questions.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. One of them contains an error. Select the segment that contains the error from the given options.

She has been speaking / to him on / the subject / many times.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. She has been speaking.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The expression "many times" indicates a completed, countable repetition, which requires the present perfect tense ("has spoken"), not the present perfect continuous ("has been speaking"). The continuous form is used for an action still in progress, not for counting occasions.

◦ Correct: She has spoken to him on the subject many times.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "to him on", "the subject" and "many times" are correct — we "speak to somebody on/about a subject".

NOTE

• Rule: with expressions of frequency/counting like "many times, several times, twice, often", use the present perfect (has/have + V3), not the perfect continuous. Perfect continuous (has been + V-ing) goes with duration expressions like "for two hours / since morning".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word 'yelling' in the given sentence.

The shouting and exclaiming gestures of Smita led to the whispering regarding her behaviour, and everyone in the party started monitoring her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. whispering.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Yelling" means shouting loudly. Its antonym is "whispering" — speaking very softly, in a hushed voice. (चिल्लाना का विलोम — फुसफुसाना)

◦ In the sentence, "the whispering regarding her behaviour" is the word opposite in meaning to "yelling".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "shouting" and Option 4 "exclaiming" are synonyms of yelling, not antonyms.

• Option 2 "monitoring" (observing/keeping watch) is unrelated to loudness of voice.

NOTE

• Loudness scale of speech verbs: whisper (softest) → murmur → speak → shout/yell/scream (loudest). Synonyms of yell: shout, scream, shriek, bawl. Antonyms: whisper, murmur, mutter.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in simple future tense form.

I loved.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. I will love.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The simple future tense is formed as: Subject + will/shall + base verb (V1). So "I loved" (simple past) becomes "I will love" in the simple future.

◦ Structure: I/We + shall/will + love; He/She/They + will + love.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "I had loved." is the past perfect tense (had + V3).

• Option 3 "I love." is the simple present tense.

• Option 4 "I shall be loving." is the future continuous tense (shall/will + be + V-ing), not the simple future.

NOTE

• Tense forms of "love": simple present — I love; simple past — I loved; simple future — I will/shall love; present perfect — I have loved; future continuous — I will be loving. SSC frequently asks direct tense-transformation questions — memorise all 12 tense structures.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Evasive
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Truthful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Evasive" means avoiding a direct answer; not frank or straightforward. Its antonym is "truthful" — honest, direct and frank. (टालमटोल करने वाला का विलोम — सत्यनिष्ठ/स्पष्टवादी)

◦ Example: The witness gave evasive replies, but the judge wanted truthful, direct answers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Elusive" (hard to catch/pin down) is close to a synonym of evasive.

• Option 1 "Obscure" (unclear/unknown) and Option 4 "Chaotic" (disorderly) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of evasive: elusive, equivocal, ambiguous, cagey, shifty. Antonyms: truthful, frank, direct, candid, straightforward.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In a small village, lived a milkmaid ______1______ sold the milk that she ____2_____ from her cows. She _____3_____ carry the milk in a big mud pitcher. One day, as she was walking _____4_____ the big pitcher full of milk on her head, she started to imagine all the things she wished to do with the money she would _____5______ from selling the milk.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. who.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a relative pronoun referring to a person ("a milkmaid") and acting as the subject of the verb "sold". "Who" is used for persons as the subject of a relative clause. (व्यक्ति के लिए 'who')

◦ Correct: ... lived a milkmaid who sold the milk that she got from her cows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "whose" shows possession (whose cows) — a noun must follow it.

• Option 2 "which" is used for animals and things, not persons.

• Option 4 "that" can refer to persons, but "who" is the most appropriate and standard choice for a person as subject, especially after a comma-free defining clause about a human being.

NOTE

• Relative pronouns: who (person — subject), whom (person — object), whose (possession), which (things/animals), that (persons/things in defining clauses).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In a small village, lived a milkmaid ______1______ sold the milk that she ____2_____ from her cows. She _____3_____ carry the milk in a big mud pitcher. One day, as she was walking _____4_____ the big pitcher full of milk on her head, she started to imagine all the things she wished to do with the money she would _____5______ from selling the milk.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. got.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The milkmaid obtained the milk from her own cows, so "got" (obtained/received) is the most appropriate verb. (प्राप्त करती थी)

◦ Correct: ... sold the milk that she got from her cows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "bought" (purchased) is wrong — she does not purchase milk from her own cows.

• Option 2 "brought" (carried to a place) does not suit "from her cows" in the sense of obtaining.

• Option 4 "drank" contradicts the passage — she sold the milk; she did not drink it.

NOTE

• Confusing pair: "bought" (past of buy — खरीदा) vs "brought" (past of bring — लाया). In cloze tests, always pick the verb that matches the logic of the passage.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In a small village, lived a milkmaid ______1______ sold the milk that she ____2_____ from her cows. She _____3_____ carry the milk in a big mud pitcher. One day, as she was walking _____4_____ the big pitcher full of milk on her head, she started to imagine all the things she wished to do with the money she would _____5______ from selling the milk.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. would.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage is a narration in the past tense ("lived", "sold", "got"). "Would" is used to describe a habitual/repeated action in the past — she used to carry the milk regularly. (भूतकाल की आदत — 'would')

◦ Correct: She would carry the milk in a big mud pitcher.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "should" expresses advice/obligation — not a past habit.

• Option 2 "will" is a future/present modal and clashes with the past narration.

• Option 3 "can" expresses present ability; its past form "could" would at least match the tense, but the sense needed here is habit, not ability.

NOTE

• Past habits are expressed by "used to" or "would": "She would carry / used to carry the milk every morning." In a past-tense narrative, keep all modals in past form (will→would, can→could, may→might).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In a small village, lived a milkmaid ______1______ sold the milk that she ____2_____ from her cows. She _____3_____ carry the milk in a big mud pitcher. One day, as she was walking _____4_____ the big pitcher full of milk on her head, she started to imagine all the things she wished to do with the money she would _____5______ from selling the milk.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "With" indicates accompaniment — she was walking along with the big pitcher (carrying it) on her head. (साथ — 'with')

◦ Correct: ... as she was walking with the big pitcher full of milk on her head ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "on" is already used later in the phrase ("on her head") and cannot show accompaniment here.

• Option 3 "in" (inside) and Option 4 "by" (agent/means) do not convey carrying something along.

NOTE

• "With" for accompaniment/possession: "walking with a stick", "a girl with a basket on her head". Preposition-based cloze blanks are best solved by reading the complete phrase: "walking with the pitcher ... on her head".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In a small village, lived a milkmaid ______1______ sold the milk that she ____2_____ from her cows. She _____3_____ carry the milk in a big mud pitcher. One day, as she was walking _____4_____ the big pitcher full of milk on her head, she started to imagine all the things she wished to do with the money she would _____5______ from selling the milk.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. earn.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Earn" means to get money in return for work or by selling something. The milkmaid imagined the money she would earn from selling the milk. (कमाना)

◦ Correct: ... all the things she wished to do with the money she would earn from selling the milk.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "catch" (to seize something moving), Option 2 "dig" (to excavate) and Option 4 "throw" (to hurl) make no sense with "money ... from selling the milk".

NOTE

• Collocation: we earn money/a living/respect; we make money; we win a prize. "Earn from selling" is the natural collocation here. The passage is from the famous fable "The Milkmaid and Her Pail" — moral: do not count your chickens before they hatch.

question: Padma awardee Arjun Singh Dhurve is related to which of the following folk dances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Baiga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Arjun Singh Dhurve, a Padma Shri awardee (2022) from Madhya Pradesh, is a renowned exponent of the Baiga folk dance — the traditional dance of the Baiga tribe. (बैगा लोक नृत्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Baiga are a particularly vulnerable tribal group (PVTG) living mainly in the Mandla, Dindori and Balaghat regions of Madhya Pradesh and parts of Chhattisgarh.

• Garba is a folk dance of Gujarat; Chhau is a semi-classical dance of Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha (Seraikela, Purulia and Mayurbhanj styles); Raslila is associated with Uttar Pradesh (Braj region) and Manipur.

NOTE

• Folk dances of Madhya Pradesh: Baiga, Matki, Gaur, Phulpati, Grida, Maanch. SSC frequently asks Padma awardees linked with folk/classical art forms.

question: Which of the following awards is NOT conferred for excellence in dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lalit Kala Akademi Award.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Lalit Kala Akademi Award is conferred for excellence in the visual/fine arts — painting, sculpture, printmaking, photography etc. — NOT for dance. (ललित कला अकादमी — दृश्य कलाओं के लिए)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is India's highest national honour for performing arts — music, dance and drama (Akademi established in 1952-53).

• The Kalidas Samman is a prestigious arts award of the Madhya Pradesh government, given in classical music, classical dance, theatre and plastic arts.

• The Padma Shri is a national civilian award that is regularly conferred on dancers and other artists.

NOTE

• The three national Akademis: Sangeet Natak Akademi (performing arts), Lalit Kala Akademi (visual arts) and Sahitya Akademi (literature) — all set up in the early 1950s in New Delhi.

question: The 'Rath Yatra' festival of Puri is celebrated as the sacred journey of which of the following Hindu deities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Jagannath.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous Rath Yatra of Puri (Odisha) celebrates the sacred annual journey of Lord Jagannath (a form of Lord Vishnu/Krishna), along with his elder brother Balabhadra and sister Subhadra, from the Jagannath Temple to the Gundicha Temple. (जगन्नाथ रथ यात्रा — पुरी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The festival is held on the Dwitiya of Ashadha Shukla Paksha (June–July); the three deities travel in three huge wooden chariots — Jagannath's chariot is called Nandighosha.

• The Jagannath Temple, Puri, was built in the 12th century by the Eastern Ganga king Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva; it is one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites (Puri, Dwarka, Badrinath, Rameswaram).

NOTE

• The English word "juggernaut" (an unstoppable force) is derived from "Jagannath", from the massive chariots of the Puri Rath Yatra.

question: Which of the following are the amounts of nutrients in a keto diet?
option_1: Only taking high number of vitamins and minerals
option_2: High protein and fat, carbohydrates in a low amount
option_3: High amount of fat, adequate protein and low carbohydrate
option_4: High carbohydrate, proper amount of protein and low fat
solution_text:
The correct answer is High amount of fat, adequate protein and low carbohydrate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A ketogenic (keto) diet is a diet with a high amount of fat, adequate (moderate) protein and very low carbohydrate. (उच्च वसा, पर्याप्त प्रोटीन, कम कार्बोहाइड्रेट)

• When carbohydrate intake is very low, the body burns fat for energy, producing ketone bodies in the liver — a state called ketosis, which gives the diet its name.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A typical keto ratio is roughly 70–75% fat, 20% protein and 5–10% carbohydrate.

• The keto diet was originally developed in the 1920s to help manage epilepsy in children; today it is popular for weight loss.

NOTE

• Macronutrients: carbohydrates and proteins give about 4 kcal/g, while fats give about 9 kcal/g. Vitamins and minerals are micronutrients — needed in small amounts.

question: The element with atomic number 59 lies in which block of the Periodic Table?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The f-block.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The element with atomic number 59 is Praseodymium (Pr), a member of the lanthanide series — hence it lies in the f-block of the Periodic Table. (परमाणु क्रमांक 59 — प्रेसियोडिमियम, f-ब्लॉक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The f-block consists of the lanthanides (Ce, at. no. 58, to Lu, at. no. 71) and the actinides (Th, at. no. 90, to Lr, at. no. 103), placed separately at the bottom of the table.

• s-block: Groups 1 and 2 (alkali and alkaline earth metals); p-block: Groups 13–18; d-block: Groups 3–12 (transition metals).

NOTE

• Lanthanides are also called rare earth elements; f-block elements are known as inner transition elements. The Modern Periodic Table (Moseley) arranges elements by increasing atomic number.

question: Which book has been authored by Rabindra Bharali?
option_2: The Forgotten Forms of Hindustani Music
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Forgotten Forms of Hindustani Music.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Forgotten Forms of Hindustani Music" has been authored by Rabindra Bharali, a noted musician and musicologist. The book documents rare and vanishing forms/genres of Hindustani classical music. (हिंदुस्तानी संगीत की विस्मृत विधाएँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Hindustani music is the classical music tradition of North India; the classical tradition of South India is Carnatic music.

• Major Hindustani vocal forms include Dhrupad, Khayal, Thumri, Tappa and Tarana.

NOTE

• "The Music Room" is a well-known book by Namita Devidayal. Books-and-authors questions on music/arts are common in SSC GK — link each book with its author and field.

question: Andal was one of the most famous women ___________ saints.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alvar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Andal (also spelt Antal) was the only woman saint among the twelve Alvars — the Tamil poet-saints devoted to Lord Vishnu — who flourished in South India roughly between the 6th and 9th centuries CE. (आंडाल — अलवार संत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Andal's celebrated Tamil devotional compositions are the "Tiruppavai" and the "Nachiyar Tirumoli"; she is worshipped at Srivilliputtur (Tamil Nadu).

• The Alvars were Vaishnavite saints; their hymns are compiled in the "Divya Prabandham" (the 'Tamil Veda').

• The Nayanars were 63 Shaivite saints devoted to Lord Shiva; the famous woman Nayanar was Karaikkal Ammaiyar.

NOTE

• The Alvar–Nayanar tradition of Tamil Nadu marked the beginning of the Bhakti movement, which later spread to North India.

question: The original non-metamorphic rock that undergoes profound physical or chemical changes leading to the formation of a metamorphic rock is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Protolith.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "protolith" (also called the parent rock) is the original, non-metamorphic rock from which a metamorphic rock is formed after undergoing profound physical or chemical changes due to heat, pressure or chemically active fluids. (मूल/जनक शैल — प्रोटोलिथ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Examples of protolith → metamorphic rock: limestone → marble; sandstone → quartzite; shale → slate; granite → gneiss; coal → graphite/anthracite.

• Regolith is the loose layer of weathered rock and soil covering bedrock; Bedrock is the solid rock beneath soil/regolith; Laterite is a residual soil/rock formed by intense leaching in hot, humid climates.

NOTE

• Rocks are of three types: igneous (from magma/lava), sedimentary (from deposition of sediments) and metamorphic (changed form). The process of transformation is called metamorphism.

question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty mentioned in the Indian constitution?
option_1: To obey parents and discharge our family responsibilities
option_2: To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, National Anthem
option_3: To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom
option_4: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is To obey parents and discharge our family responsibilities.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "To obey parents and discharge our family responsibilities" is NOT a Fundamental Duty listed in Article 51A of the Indian Constitution. (मौलिक कर्तव्यों में शामिल नहीं)

• The other three options are actual Fundamental Duties: to abide by the Constitution and respect the National Flag and National Anthem — 51A(a); to cherish the noble ideals of the freedom struggle — 51A(b); to uphold the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India — 51A(c).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties were added to Part IV-A (Article 51A) by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee — originally 10 duties.

• The 86th Amendment, 2002, added the 11th duty — 51A(k): parents/guardians to provide opportunities for education to children between 6 and 14 years.

• Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR and are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts).

NOTE

• Total Fundamental Duties now: 11. Remember: duties apply only to citizens, not to foreigners.

question: Which bonding material was mainly used to join the stones or bricks of 'The Great Bath' of the Harappan Civilisation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gypsum Mortar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The bricks of "The Great Bath" at Mohenjo-daro were set with gypsum mortar (plaster), and the structure was made watertight with a layer of bitumen (natural tar) along with finely fitted burnt bricks. (महास्नानागार — जिप्सम मोर्टार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Great Bath is a large rectangular tank in the citadel area of Mohenjo-daro (now in Sindh, Pakistan), measuring about 12 m x 7 m and 2.4 m deep, probably used for ritual bathing.

• Mohenjo-daro ("Mound of the Dead") was excavated by R. D. Banerji in 1922; it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• Harappan structures used burnt bricks in a standard ratio of 4:2:1. Other famous structures: the Great Granary (Harappa/Mohenjo-daro) and the Dockyard at Lothal.

question: Which of the following is NOT a cropping season in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fang.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India has three cropping seasons — Kharif, Rabi and Zaid. "Fang" is NOT a cropping season. (फांग — कोई फसल ऋतु नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kharif crops are sown with the onset of the monsoon (June–July) and harvested in September–October — rice, maize, jowar, bajra, cotton, groundnut, soyabean.

• Rabi crops are sown in winter (October–December) and harvested in summer (April–June) — wheat, barley, gram, peas, mustard.

• Zaid is the short summer season (March–June) between Rabi and Kharif — watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, vegetables and fodder crops.

NOTE

• "Kharif" and "Rabi" are Arabic words meaning "autumn" and "spring" respectively (referring to the harvest time). India's cropping pattern is heavily dependent on the south-west monsoon.

question: In January 2023, who was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Bihar for the ninth time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitish Kumar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nitish Kumar (Janata Dal-United) holds the record of being sworn in as the Chief Minister of Bihar for the ninth time. He first became CM in 2000. (नीतीश कुमार — बिहार के मुख्यमंत्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor under Article 164 of the Constitution; there is no limit on the number of times a person can become CM.

• The capital of Bihar is Patna; Bihar has a bicameral legislature (Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council).

NOTE

• Article 163 — Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor; Article 164 — appointment of CM and other ministers by the Governor. The CM is the real executive head of the state government.

question:
Which of the following options correctly matches column-A with column-B?

Column-A (Name of Vitamin) — Column-B (Deficiency Diseases)

i. Vitamin A — a. Scurvy

ii. Vitamin D — b. Beriberi

iii. Vitamin B1 — c. Rickets

iv. Vitamin C — d. Night Blindness
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct matching of vitamins with their deficiency diseases is:

◦ Vitamin A → Night Blindness (i-d) — रतौंधी

◦ Vitamin D → Rickets (ii-c) — सूखा रोग/रिकेट्स

◦ Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) → Beriberi (iii-b) — बेरी-बेरी

◦ Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) → Scurvy (iv-a) — स्कर्वी

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Vitamin A (Retinol) — needed for vision; deficiency causes night blindness and xerophthalmia; sources: carrots, papaya, fish liver oil.

• Vitamin D (Calciferol) — helps calcium absorption; deficiency causes rickets (children) and osteomalacia (adults); made in the skin in sunlight.

• Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) — deficiency causes beriberi (weakness, nerve damage); sources: whole grains, pulses.

• Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) — deficiency causes scurvy (bleeding gums); sources: citrus fruits, amla.

NOTE

• Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K; water-soluble vitamins: B-complex and C. Vitamin B12 deficiency causes pernicious anaemia; Vitamin K deficiency delays blood clotting.

question: Who is the chairman of the State Planning Board?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chief Minister.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Chief Minister of the state is the ex-officio chairman of the State Planning Board/Commission, the apex planning body at the state level. (राज्य योजना बोर्ड का अध्यक्ष — मुख्यमंत्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Similarly, at the national level, the Prime Minister is the ex-officio chairman of NITI Aayog (which replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015).

• The Governor is the constitutional head of the state; the Advocate General (Article 165) is the highest law officer of the state; the Speaker presides over the Legislative Assembly.

NOTE

• At the district level, planning is done by the District Planning Committee (Article 243ZD). The PM also chairs the Governing Council of NITI Aayog, which includes all state CMs.

question: Magnolia and Laurel trees are found in which type of forest in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Montane Forests.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Magnolia and Laurel are evergreen broad-leaf trees of the Montane (mountain) Forests — specifically the wet temperate forests found at altitudes of about 1000–2000 m in hilly regions of India. (पर्वतीय वन — मैगनोलिया और लॉरेल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• In montane forests, between 1500–3000 m, temperate coniferous trees like pine, deodar, silver fir, spruce and cedar dominate; at higher altitudes come alpine vegetation (silver fir, junipers, birches) and then alpine grasslands.

• Tropical Thorn Forests (rainfall below 70 cm) have acacias, cacti and euphorbias; Mangrove Forests (deltas/coasts) have sundari trees; Tropical Deciduous Forests (monsoon forests) have teak, sal and sandalwood.

NOTE

• Montane forests in India occur in the Himalayas and in the Nilgiris/Western Ghats (where the high-altitude forests are called Sholas).

question: According to the Census of India 2011, what was the total population of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.21 billion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, the total population of India was about 1.21 billion (121 crore — 1,21,08,54,977). (जनगणना 2011 — लगभग 121 करोड़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Census 2011 was the 15th Census since 1872 and the 7th after Independence; its motto was "Our Census, Our Future"; the Census Commissioner was C. Chandramouli.

• Key 2011 figures: decadal growth 17.7%; sex ratio 943 females per 1000 males; literacy rate 74.04% (males 82.14%, females 65.46%); density 382 persons/sq km.

• Most populous state: Uttar Pradesh; least populous: Sikkim; India holds about 17.5% of the world's population.

NOTE

• The Census is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs (Census Act, 1948).

question: In 1927, where was the conference against colonial oppression and imperialism, in which Jawaharlal Nehru participated on behalf of Indian National Congress, held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brussels.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In February 1927, the Congress of Oppressed Nationalities (League against Imperialism and Colonial Oppression) was held at Brussels (Belgium). Jawaharlal Nehru attended it on behalf of the Indian National Congress. (ब्रुसेल्स सम्मेलन, 1927)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Brussels Congress brought together representatives of colonised nations of Asia, Africa and Latin America; Nehru was elected to the Executive Council of the League against Imperialism formed there.

• The visit deepened Nehru's interest in socialism and international anti-imperialist movements; in the same year he also visited the Soviet Union.

NOTE

• Soon after, at the Madras Session of the INC (1927), presided over by M. A. Ansari, the Congress passed a resolution on complete independence moved by Nehru. Bruges, Leuven and Antwerp are other cities of Belgium.

question: Duare Ration Scheme, which has been deemed legally void by the high court, was launched by which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Duare Ration" (Ration at the Doorstep) scheme was launched by the West Bengal government in 2021 to deliver foodgrains under the Public Distribution System (PDS) at the doorstep of beneficiaries. (दुआरे राशन — पश्चिम बंगाल)

• The Calcutta High Court declared the scheme legally void, holding it beyond the scope of the National Food Security Act, 2013.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Duare" means "at the doorstep" in Bengali; it followed the state's wider "Duare Sarkar" (government at the doorstep) outreach programme.

• The National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 provides subsidised foodgrains (rice at Rs.3/kg, wheat Rs.2/kg, coarse grains Rs.1/kg) to about two-thirds of the population through the Targeted PDS.

NOTE

• Other West Bengal schemes: Lakshmir Bhandar (income support to women), Kanyashree (girls' education), Swasthya Sathi (health cover).

question: Which reform was initiated by Lord Ripon for the welfare of labourers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Factory Act.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lord Ripon (Viceroy of India, 1880–1884) enacted the first Factory Act in 1881 for the welfare of labourers. It prohibited employment of children below 7 years, limited working hours of children, and provided for fencing of dangerous machinery. (प्रथम कारखाना अधिनियम, 1881 — लॉर्ड रिपन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Lord Ripon is called the "Father of Local Self-Government in India" for his Resolution of 1882 on local self-government.

• He repealed the Vernacular Press Act (1882) — the Act itself had been passed by Lord Lytton in 1878; Ripon also appointed the Hunter Commission (1882) on education and introduced the first regular Census in 1881.

• The Ilbert Bill controversy (1883) also occurred during his tenure.

NOTE

• The second Factory Act (1891), under Lord Lansdowne, raised the minimum age of child employment to 9 years and provided a weekly holiday for workers.

question: The Ashokan inscriptions of Afghanistan are written in Aramaic and ________ scripts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Greek.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ashokan inscriptions found in Afghanistan (e.g., the bilingual rock inscription at Kandahar) are written in the Aramaic and Greek scripts/languages. (अफगानिस्तान — अरामाइक और यूनानी लिपि)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ashoka's inscriptions in the Indian subcontinent are mostly in the Prakrit language and Brahmi script; in the north-west (Pakistan region) they are in Kharosthi script (written right to left).

• Ashokan Brahmi was first deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837.

• Ashoka (Mauryan ruler, c. 268–232 BCE) issued 14 Major Rock Edicts, Minor Rock Edicts and 7 Pillar Edicts; the Kalinga War (c. 261 BCE) is described in Rock Edict XIII.

NOTE

• Scripts of Ashokan edicts: Brahmi (most of India), Kharosthi (north-west), Greek and Aramaic (Afghanistan). Devanagari, Sharda and Ol Chiki are much later scripts (Ol Chiki is used for Santali).

question: As per Census of India 2011, which of the following states has the highest child sex ratio (in the age group of 0-6 years)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mizoram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, among the given states, Mizoram recorded the highest child sex ratio (0–6 years) — about 970 girls per 1000 boys. (मिज़ोरम — सर्वाधिक शिशु लिंगानुपात)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The national child sex ratio (0–6 years) in 2011 was 919 (down from 927 in 2001) — the lowest since Independence at that time.

• The lowest child sex ratio among states was in Haryana (834).

• The highest overall sex ratio (all ages) was in Kerala (1084); among UTs, Daman & Diu had the lowest.

NOTE

• Child sex ratio = number of girls per 1000 boys in the 0–6 age group. Schemes like "Beti Bachao Beti Padhao" (2015) were launched to address the declining child sex ratio.

question: Who became the first Indian woman to be inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Diana Edulji.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Diana Edulji, the former captain of the Indian women's cricket team, became the first Indian woman cricketer to be inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame (in 2023). (डायना एडुल्जी — आईसीसी हॉल ऑफ फेम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Diana Edulji was a left-arm spinner who led India in Tests and ODIs in the 1970s–80s; she was also a member of the Supreme Court-appointed Committee of Administrators (CoA) of the BCCI and received the Arjuna Award (1983) and Padma Shri (2002).

• Indian men in the ICC Hall of Fame include Bishan Singh Bedi, Kapil Dev, Sunil Gavaskar, Anil Kumble, Rahul Dravid, Sachin Tendulkar, Vinoo Mankad and Virender Sehwag.

NOTE

• The ICC (International Cricket Council), headquartered in Dubai (UAE), launched the Hall of Fame in 2009 in association with FICA to honour the legends of the game.

question: How many gold medals did Maharashtra win to top the medal tally at the 37th National Games event held in Goa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 80.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the 37th National Games, held in Goa (October–November 2023), Maharashtra topped the medal tally with 80 gold medals (228 total medals). (37वें राष्ट्रीय खेल — महाराष्ट्र, 80 स्वर्ण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Services Sports Control Board finished second in the tally, followed by Haryana.

• The 37th National Games were the first National Games hosted by Goa; the mascot was "Moga" (meaning 'love' in Konkani).

• The 38th National Games (2025) were held in Uttarakhand.

NOTE

• The National Games of India are organised by the Indian Olympic Association (IOA); the first Games (as Indian Olympic Games) were held in 1924 at Lahore.

question: Who among the following personalities from the Carnatic Music correctly represent the 'Trinity of Carnatic Music'?
option_2: Manambuchavadi Venkatasubbayyar, Tyagaraja and Muthuswami Dikshitar
option_3: MS Subbalakshmi, DK Pattammal and ML Vasanthakumari
option_4: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Trinity of Carnatic Music" (Carnatic Sangita Trimurti) comprises Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri — the three great composer-saints of the 18th–19th centuries, all born at Tiruvarur (Tamil Nadu). (कर्नाटक संगीत की त्रिमूर्ति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Tyagaraja composed thousands of devotional kritis in Telugu, mostly in praise of Lord Rama — the famous Pancharatna Kritis; the Tyagaraja Aradhana festival is held annually at Thiruvaiyaru.

• Muthuswami Dikshitar composed in Sanskrit (signature "Guruguha"); Syama Sastri composed mainly on Goddess Kamakshi (signature "Syama Krishna").

• Purandara Dasa (16th century) is honoured as the "Pitamaha (grandfather) of Carnatic music"; M. S. Subbulakshmi, D. K. Pattammal and M. L. Vasanthakumari are called the "female trinity" of Carnatic music.

NOTE

• Carnatic music is the classical music of South India; its basic elements are raga (melody) and tala (rhythm). M. S. Subbulakshmi was the first musician to receive the Bharat Ratna (1998).

question: Revenue account includes items related to the _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is all of the given options.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the official answer key, the revenue account includes items related to all of the given options — i.e., items may pertain to the current financial year as well as adjustments such as arrears of the previous financial year and receipts/payments relating to the next financial year recorded during the year. (राजस्व खाता)

• The revenue account of the budget consists of revenue receipts (tax revenue like income tax, GST, excise; and non-tax revenue like interest, dividends, fees) and revenue expenditure (salaries, pensions, subsidies, interest payments) — items that do not create assets or reduce liabilities.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The government budget (Article 112 — Annual Financial Statement) has two accounts: the Revenue Account and the Capital Account.

• Capital account items either create assets or cause a change in liabilities — e.g., loans, disinvestment, capital expenditure on infrastructure.

• Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure − Revenue receipts; Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure − Total receipts excluding borrowings.

NOTE

• Revenue receipts are recurring in nature and do not have to be repaid, whereas capital receipts (like borrowings) create liabilities or reduce assets.
